name: G2 Max
summary: The G2 Max is a safety-certified heavy-duty industrial robot launched on October 26 (2026) and aimed at depalletizing, material handling and production line feeding. It has 7-DOF force-controlled dual arms with a 20 kg single-arm load and is said to be operating on multiple production lines. It is a variant in AgiBot's wheeled G2 line.
sensors: 360° multimodal perception and protection: 2D/3D LiDAR, ultrasonic sensors, chassis safety edges, physical emergency stops; vision guidance and dual-arm force control.
highlights: Single-arm load 20 kg, dual-arm rated 40 kg, dual-arm peak up to 50 kg; arm repeatability ≤±0.5mm.
7-DOF force-controlled dual arm with vision guidance.
Vertical working area 0.1m-2.5m, horizontal working area 1.2m, with a waist-tilt joint for single-sided palletizing and depalletizing.
Dual-battery hot-swappable design with autonomous recharging for 24/7 operation.
Can unpalletize 80 boxes and palletize 75 boxes per hour in e-commerce warehousing.
Compatible with the Genie Studio 2.0 platform.
Used on the Qiyuan T1 production line to move joint parts.
caveats: Height, weight, total DOF, hand DOF, speed, runtime, compute and price are not stated in the sources.
Purchase path is an assumption: no source describes how to buy the G2 Max.
The G2 Max is described only in a republished EEWorld article, with no official AgiBot page among the sources.
Status 'pilot' is inferred from the claim that it operates on multiple production lines; commercial availability is not confirmed.
Other sources cover the standard AgiBot G2 (wheeled, with different specs), not the Max variant.
The Unitree G2 Ultra in s6 is an unrelated product.
